en.title: Dead Cells Director's Brutal Roguelike Tenjutsu Returns with 2027 Switch 2 Launch
en.summary: After years of silence, Tenjutsu, the ambitious roguelike from Sébastien Benard, the former director of Dead Cells, has resurfaced with a new trailer and a 2027 release window. This gritty 2D brawler will be available on PC and the upcoming Nintendo Switch 2.
en.body:
Remember **Tenjutsu**? This 2D pixel brawler, helmed by **Sébastien Benard**, the creative force behind the beloved roguelike **Dead Cells**, seemed to vanish after its initial announcement. Now, after a significant period of quiet, the game has roared back to life with a brand-new trailer and a confirmed 2027 release window. Fans of challenging, action-packed indie titles have reason to be excited, as **Tenjutsu** is slated to launch not only on PC but also on the forthcoming **Nintendo Switch 2**, signaling a strong commitment to bringing this intense experience to a wider audience.

The latest gameplay showcase offers a visceral glimpse into what made **Tenjutsu** stand out initially. Players will step into the shoes of **Ten**, a former Yakuza recently released from prison. Her path to a clean slate is brutally interrupted by the ruthless bosses of Kuroboro City, who clearly have other plans for her. The core loop appears to be a frantic, skill-based 2D combat experience where **Ten** unleashes devastating hand-to-hand and weapon-based attacks. Each run through the procedurally generated city promises a unique challenge, with randomized layouts and a deep progression system. Collecting tattooed teeth serves as a novel currency, unlocking new skills, potent weapons, and other vital benefits. The game also appears to feature all the expected conveniences of a modern roguelike, including healing mechanics, vending machines stocked with items, and various shop offerings to aid players on their perilous journey.

## A Gritty Tale of Redemption and Revenge

The narrative premise of **Tenjutsu** immediately sets a dark and compelling tone. **Ten's** struggle to escape her past while being dragged back into the underworld by her former associates provides a strong motivation for players. This blend of personal redemption and violent confrontation against a corrupt city is a narrative trope that resonates deeply within the gaming community, especially when paired with challenging, skill-testing gameplay. The connection to **Sébastien Benard's** previous work on **Dead Cells** also carries significant weight. **Dead Cells** is celebrated for its tight controls, satisfying combat, and deep replayability, elements that fans will undoubtedly be hoping to see mirrored and expanded upon in **Tenjutsu**. The prospect of experiencing this unique combat system on the **Nintendo Switch 2** adds another layer of anticipation for those who enjoy gaming on the go.

## What Fans Can Expect

The return of **Tenjutsu** is a significant event for fans of challenging indie games and the roguelike genre. The pedigree of **Sébastien Benard** alone is enough to generate substantial buzz, and the promise of brutal, stylish combat combined with procedural generation and a compelling narrative sets high expectations. The confirmation of a **Nintendo Switch 2** release is also a major point of interest, suggesting that the game is being designed with the flexibility and power of next-generation portable hardware in mind. While **Motion Twin**, the studio behind **Dead Cells**, has been busy with titles like **Castlevania: Belmont's Curse** and the early access **Windblown**, this new venture from their former director demonstrates the continued innovation within the studio's sphere.

## What's Next

While a precise release date remains unannounced, the 2027 window provides a clear target for eager players. Further details on **Tenjutsu's** gameplay mechanics, narrative progression, and the full scope of its content are expected in the coming months, offering more opportunities to delve into this promising roguelike.

content_raw: Remember Tenjutsu , a 2D pixel brawler helmed by former Dead Cells director Sébastien Benard? After seemingly falling off the face of the Earth for all these years, it’s received a new trailer and a 2027 release window. If that wasn’t enough, Nintendo Switch 2 players can get their hands on it alongside PC. The latest gameplay trailer showcases what made Tenjutsu stand out in the first place: Protagonist Ten, a former Yakuza recently released from prison, taking fools to school with brutal hand-to-hand (and oftentimes, head-to-face) knockouts. Though seeking to leave her criminal past behind, Kuroboro City’s bosses have other ideas. As you explore the city, each run randomised, you’ll pick up new skills to unleash on foes. New weapons also await, and depending on how you utilize the progression system (which relies on collecting tattooed teeth), you can unlock other benefits. Healing, vending machines with items, shop offerings – the works. Stay tuned for more details in the coming months and a concrete release date (hopefully). As for Motion Twin, the studio that developed Dead Cells , it recently released Castlevania: Belmont’s Curse , a new title in Konami’s long-running Metroidvania series. It’s also working on Windblown , an isometric rogue-lite hack-and-slash that’s currently in early access. Take a new look at Tenjutsu, a gritty combat roguelike where you’ll step into the shoes of a renegade yakuza determined to defy her former associates.
